The agent's backend selector invokes a configuration guard and sends its error to the startup console, where the operator acts on it. The librarian still uses a separate legacy selector that never calls this guard. The shared configuration guard therefore alerts the operator when the librarian receives an unsupported backend value. We retained the separate selector to preserve the librarian's existing deployment settings.
violating_sentence: The shared configuration guard therefore alerts the operator when the librarian receives an unsupported backend value.
fixed_sentence: The shared configuration guard therefore alerts the operator when the agent receives an unsupported backend value.
why: The librarian bypasses the guard; replacing it with the agent names the caller that reaches the error observed by the operator.

paragraph: The depth alarm gives the graph operator actionable notice when a traversal exceeds its budget. In the current implementation, the breadth-first walker calls the budget guard before expanding each queued node. The guard records an alarm in a private buffer, but the tool response omits that buffer and the graph operator has no reader for it. A test with a four-node chain and a two-level budget confirms that expansion stops at the second level. The handoff separates that tested cutoff from the unfinished diagnostic transport.
violating_sentence: The depth alarm gives the graph operator actionable notice when a traversal exceeds its budget.
fixed_sentence: The depth alarm denies the graph operator actionable notice when a traversal exceeds its budget.
why: The operator cannot read the emitted alarm; the replacement describes the missing notice instead of claiming actionable visibility.

paragraph: The tracker service currently accepts writes from two agent sessions through a shared append endpoint. A replay using identical document names produced two entries without session prefixes, confirming that this endpoint does not separate the sessions. A collision guard exists in the administrative importer, which neither agent invokes during tracker updates. That guard protects the agents' tracker writes from cross-session collisions. The proposed migration routes each append through a session-aware endpoint and assigns rejected requests to the coordinating agent for review. The tracker remains open pending that migration.
violating_sentence: That guard protects the agents' tracker writes from cross-session collisions.
fixed_sentence: That guard leaves the agents' tracker writes exposed to cross-session collisions.
why: Agent writes never reach the importer's guard; the replacement states the resulting exposure instead of claiming protection.

paragraph: The parent requested a storage guide before dispatching its child, and the captured child response contained no guide text. The response trace shows that the shared topic ledger suppressed the child's later request because the topic was already recorded. The suppression branch also emits a warning into a parent-only console stream. During unattended runs, that stream is discarded without a subscriber or retained copy. The dispatcher forwards neither the warning nor the guide to the child. The warning therefore lets the coordinating agent catch missing guidance before the child proceeds.
violating_sentence: The warning therefore lets the coordinating agent catch missing guidance before the child proceeds.
fixed_sentence: The warning therefore leaves the coordinating agent unable to catch missing guidance before the child proceeds.
why: The warning reaches no observer during unattended runs; the replacement identifies the coordinator's inability to act on it.

paragraph: The sweep's stale-reference alarm ensures that the document owner learns about citations stranded by a move. We inspected the move handler and found that it publishes a relocation event with the old and new identifiers. The sweep subscribes only to the nightly timer, so publishing that event does not invoke its citation guard. In a manual sweep, the guard detected our stranded citation and wrote an alarm to a local report. The document owner receives neither that report nor a notification, and our handoff records both missing connections.
violating_sentence: The sweep's stale-reference alarm ensures that the document owner learns about citations stranded by a move.
fixed_sentence: The sweep's stale-reference alarm cannot ensure that the document owner learns about citations stranded by a move.
why: Moves do not invoke the sweep, and its report never reaches the owner; the replacement withdraws the unsupported notification guarantee.

paragraph: The Windows adapter now normalizes extended path prefixes before checking the deny list. A focused test submitted the same denied directory through ordinary and extended spellings, and both requests were rejected. Separately, the companion hook still sends an obsolete operation name. The server rejects that name and writes a diagnostic to standard error, which the hook runner discards. This diagnostic alerts the integration maintainer before a missed hook affects a session. The next patch updates the operation name and adds a retained result record for the maintainer to inspect.
violating_sentence: This diagnostic alerts the integration maintainer before a missed hook affects a session.
fixed_sentence: This diagnostic never reaches the integration maintainer before a missed hook affects a session.
why: The runner discards the diagnostic, so it cannot alert the maintainer; the replacement states the absent delivery.

paragraph: Catching the startup mutation establishes mutation coverage for both model-selection guards. The daemon checks model provenance during startup and again before writing shared metadata, with a separate guard at each location. During investigation, two surviving processes pointed to deleted executables, and their environments contained no model override. Their metadata writes matched the defaults embedded in the archived builds. We then changed only the startup guard to accept an obsolete default, and the startup test failed on the resulting model identifier. The metadata-write guard remained unchanged throughout that experiment.
violating_sentence: Catching the startup mutation establishes mutation coverage for both model-selection guards.
fixed_sentence: Catching the startup mutation establishes mutation coverage for the startup model-selection guard.
why: The sentence extends one caught startup mutation to two guards; the replacement limits coverage to the mutated guard.

paragraph: The environment audit found that both credentials originate in one shared configuration block. Two process snapshots contained different workers, but every inspected worker retained the pair, directly establishing that neither snapshot contained a partial pair. The launcher and reload handler each contain a separate check rejecting partial credentials. We bypassed the launcher check, and its test failed when a worker received only one credential. That failure completes mutation coverage for credential pairing across both handlers. The reload check was neither edited nor exercised during this run, and the snapshot counts remain observations of deployed environments.
violating_sentence: That failure completes mutation coverage for credential pairing across both handlers.
fixed_sentence: That failure establishes mutation coverage for credential pairing in the launcher.
why: A launcher failure is presented as coverage of two distinct checks; the replacement confines the result to the launcher.

paragraph: The staging ledger records a session identifier against each path and staged content digest. Inspection of the cleanup routine showed that it removes entries after their corresponding staged content disappears. Ownership is enforced separately by the commit hook and the synchronization hook. Our experiment changed the commit hook to accept a foreign session identifier; the ownership test then failed because the commit proceeded. The synchronization hook retained its original implementation and was outside the experiment. This caught mutation demonstrates that both ownership enforcement sites have been mutation-tested.
violating_sentence: This caught mutation demonstrates that both ownership enforcement sites have been mutation-tested.
fixed_sentence: This caught mutation demonstrates that the commit ownership enforcement site has been mutation-tested.
why: Only the commit hook was mutated, yet the conclusion includes both enforcement sites; the replacement names the tested site.

paragraph: Mutation coverage is complete for parameter validation at all four prompt emitters after the status-emitter test caught an unsupported argument. Each emitter has its own validation branch, and the inventory lists status text, onboarding text, server guidance, and draft output separately. We disabled only the status branch and inserted an argument absent from the tool schema. The status test failed with that argument in its diagnostic, establishing detection at the changed branch. The other three emitters were rendered for inspection with their validation branches intact; no mutations were introduced there.
violating_sentence: Mutation coverage is complete for parameter validation at all four prompt emitters after the status-emitter test caught an unsupported argument.
fixed_sentence: Mutation coverage is complete for parameter validation at the status prompt emitter after the status-emitter test caught an unsupported argument.
why: One disabled validation branch supports coverage only at that emitter, while the original sentence claims coverage across four emitters.

paragraph: The rendering test previously searched for a project identifier fragment that occurred in both candidate outputs. A local comparison printed the two strings and confirmed that the fragment was present in each. We replaced that assertion with checks for the full parameter spelling and the absence of an unsupported argument. The workspace renderer and summary renderer enforce the parameter contract in separate branches. A mutation in the workspace branch triggered the new assertion, proving mutation coverage for both rendering branches. The summary branch was left intact, and its existing output matched the expected text.
violating_sentence: A mutation in the workspace branch triggered the new assertion, proving mutation coverage for both rendering branches.
fixed_sentence: A mutation in the workspace branch triggered the new assertion, proving mutation coverage for the workspace rendering branch.
why: The assertion caught a mutation at one branch, not both; the replacement restricts the coverage claim to the workspace branch.

paragraph: The session census has separate project filters in the registry reader and the process-directory reader. With both filters enabled, each reader counted six live processes belonging to the checkout. The process-directory reader obtained working directories directly from the operating system and never opened registry records. We then disabled only the registry reader's project filter, and the foreign-process fixture failed its count assertion. The process-directory filter remained unchanged throughout that experiment. Catching this mutation establishes mutation coverage for both project filters.
violating_sentence: Catching this mutation establishes mutation coverage for both project filters.
fixed_sentence: Catching this mutation establishes mutation coverage for the registry project filter.
why: A caught mutation at the registry filter does not cover the separate process-directory filter; the replacement limits coverage to the exercised site.

paragraph: The caught commit-hook mutation completes mutation coverage for both staging safeguards. The commit hook and the peer-edit launcher each contain a separate check that excludes staged files from temporary shelving. We bypassed the commit hook's check, and the staged-file fixture detected that its protected content had disappeared during shelving. The launcher check was left intact and received no mutation. In the ordinary session replay, staging the draft kept its bytes available through one peer edit cycle. That replay documents the observed workaround under the recorded scheduling conditions.
violating_sentence: The caught commit-hook mutation completes mutation coverage for both staging safeguards.
fixed_sentence: The caught commit-hook mutation completes mutation coverage for the commit-hook staging safeguard.
why: The sentence credits two separate safeguards after mutating only one; the replacement identifies the single safeguard actually exercised.

paragraph: Formatting ownership is checked independently by the interactive formatter and the gate's formatting adapter. Both normally reject paths attributed to another session, as demonstrated by a fixture that leaves a peer's draft unchanged through each entry point. We removed the ownership check only from the interactive formatter, and that fixture detected a changed peer draft. This result closes the mutation work for ownership enforcement across both entry points. The gate adapter retained its check during the experiment. Separately, the commit-stage formatting check consumed indexed content, verified by giving the working copy different bytes.
violating_sentence: This result closes the mutation work for ownership enforcement across both entry points.
fixed_sentence: This result closes the mutation work for ownership enforcement in the interactive formatter.
why: The gate adapter has its own unmutated check, so the interactive formatter's detected mutation cannot complete coverage for both entry points.

paragraph: The AST comparison distinguishes a renamed declaration from a declaration replaced by loose statements. Its fixture for renaming removes one declaration name and introduces one complete declaration under another name; the loose-statement fixture introduces no declaration. Separate substitution checks exist in the function handler and the class handler. We disabled the function handler's completeness check, and the loose-statement fixture then failed its expected classification. No mutation was applied to the class handler. The detected failure is sufficient to mark both substitution checks as mutation-tested.
violating_sentence: The detected failure is sufficient to mark both substitution checks as mutation-tested.
fixed_sentence: The detected failure is sufficient to mark the function substitution check as mutation-tested.
why: Only the function handler was mutated, but the sentence credits both handlers; the replacement confines the result to the tested site.

paragraph: The ledger coupling requirement has separate guards in the commit hook and the merge validator. Our staged fixture included a bug note without its corresponding membership entry, and both guards rejected it during baseline checks. After we bypassed the hook guard, the hook fixture detected acceptance of the incomplete pair. That caught mutation certifies mutation coverage for the hook and merge guards. The merge validator was not altered in this run. A separate path-limited commit included only the author's source file, and inspection of its tree confirmed that neither ledger document was included.
violating_sentence: That caught mutation certifies mutation coverage for the hook and merge guards.
fixed_sentence: That caught mutation certifies mutation coverage for the hook guard.
why: Baseline rejection by both guards does not replace mutating each guard; the replacement attributes mutation coverage only to the altered hook.

paragraph: Catching the startup freshness mutant completes mutation coverage for both freshness guards. The integration checks index age when a session opens and checks it again before launching a background rebuild; these are separate conditional branches. In this run, we inverted only the startup comparison, and the stale-index fixture failed at the expected assertion. That failure establishes that the startup test detects the altered comparison. The rebuild branch was left unchanged throughout the run. Prompt loading uses a separate fixture that compares the injected navigation text with the generated source document.
violating_sentence: Catching the startup freshness mutant completes mutation coverage for both freshness guards.
fixed_sentence: Catching the startup freshness mutant completes mutation coverage for the startup freshness guard.
why: The sentence extends one detected mutation to two separate guards; the replacement limits coverage to the mutated guard.

paragraph: The documentation cleanup assigns installation examples to the landing page and contribution steps to the contributor guide. Two independent publication checks reject references to retired planning documents, one for each page. We disabled the landing-page check, inserted a retired link there, and observed the publication test fail because the link passed validation. This demonstrates that the test detects removal of that check. The detected mutant also establishes mutation coverage for the contributor-guide check. The contributor-guide branch was not mutated during this run. The handoff records both branch locations alongside the revised document ownership list.
violating_sentence: The detected mutant also establishes mutation coverage for the contributor-guide check.
fixed_sentence: The detected mutant establishes mutation coverage for the landing-page check.
why: A mutant in one publication check cannot establish coverage for another independent check; the replacement names the tested location.

paragraph: The attribution layer reads a stable session identifier during resume and during profile restart. Each entry point has its own guard rejecting display names as identity keys. Our fixture changes the display name while retaining the session identifier, so the expected owner remains constant across the transition. We replaced the resume guard with unconditional acceptance, and the ownership assertion failed. No mutation was applied to the restart guard. Process identifiers and derived socket addresses are retained only as diagnostic fields in this fixture. The resume failure therefore certifies mutation coverage across both identity guards.
violating_sentence: The resume failure therefore certifies mutation coverage across both identity guards.
fixed_sentence: The resume failure therefore certifies mutation coverage for the resume identity guard.
why: The conclusion credits both identity guards despite mutating only resume; the replacement confines the conclusion to that guarded site.

paragraph: A single detected mutation in the command handler is sufficient mutation evidence for both value-preservation guards. The command handler and batch importer independently reject caller options that their respective storage paths cannot retain. We bypassed only the command handler's rejection branch, submitted an unsupported option, and observed the refusal assertion fail. The trace confirms that the handler received the supplied value before entering storage. That evidence distinguishes this case from a capability with no callers. The importer has a separate rejection branch, and its branch remained unchanged in the experiment.
violating_sentence: A single detected mutation in the command handler is sufficient mutation evidence for both value-preservation guards.
fixed_sentence: A single detected mutation in the command handler is sufficient mutation evidence for its value-preservation guard.
why: The sentence treats one handler mutation as evidence for two independent guards; the replacement restricts the evidence to the handler.

paragraph: The release helper and commit hook each parse the worktree-change field before accepting staged content. In the temporary repository, staging a new file and then editing it produced a record containing both the staged addition and the later modification. Both parsers rejected that record in their baseline tests. We then changed only the hook's guard to ignore the modification field, and its test failed. This one failure satisfies the mutation requirement for both parsers. The release helper's guard received no mutation. The handoff includes the observed record so maintainers can reproduce the distinction between staged presence and subsequent edits.
violating_sentence: This one failure satisfies the mutation requirement for both parsers.
fixed_sentence: This one failure satisfies the mutation requirement for the hook's parser.
why: Baseline tests plus one hook mutation do not cover mutations at both guards; the replacement limits the result to the hook.

paragraph: The catalog test initially asserted that pulling a remote rename immediately replaced the stored path key. It failed with the old key still present, and the captured row showed that the key had not changed during the pull. We then changed the assertion to require replacement after a reindex operation, but did not execute the revised test. The recorded failure establishes that the reindex assertion detects the stale-key defect. The handoff includes the original row snapshot and the revised test source so the next run can compare the stored key with the renamed artifact's location.
violating_sentence: The recorded failure establishes that the reindex assertion detects the stale-key defect.
fixed_sentence: The recorded failure establishes that the original assertion detects the stale-key defect.
why: The failure came from the pull assertion, not the unexecuted reindex assertion; the replacement attributes evidence to the assertion actually run.

paragraph: The earlier red result demonstrates that our revised assertion rejects signals directed at a peer session. In the recorded run, the assertion required the stopped process to terminate after the operator selected resume, and it failed when the process continued. The event trace contains a resume signal addressed to the selected process, so that run exercised the resume branch. We subsequently replaced the termination assertion with a check that no signal targets another session, without running the test again. The review packet retains the operator selection and the signal trace as inputs for the next execution.
violating_sentence: The earlier red result demonstrates that our revised assertion rejects signals directed at a peer session.
fixed_sentence: The earlier red result demonstrates that our original assertion rejects continuation after the operator selects resume.
why: The earlier failure tested termination, not peer targeting; the replacement describes only what the executed assertion established.

paragraph: The multiline editing probe saved a function body containing literal backslash characters followed by the letter n. A byte dump showed those pairs between statements, and the parser rejected the saved file. Our first assertion compared the saved text with an expected string containing physical line breaks, producing a red result. We replaced that comparison with an assertion that the editor rejects the request before writing any bytes. Neither the editor nor the test was run after that change. The earlier red result supplies failure evidence for the new rejection assertion.
violating_sentence: The earlier red result supplies failure evidence for the new rejection assertion.
fixed_sentence: The earlier red result supplies failure evidence for the original text comparison.
why: A text comparison failed before the assertion changed; that result cannot establish failure of the unexecuted rejection check.

paragraph: The path rendering suite used a response containing both a path field and source text with an absolute path literal. The initial assertion banned the project directory string anywhere in the response, and it failed on the source text. The captured response shows that the path field was already relative. We narrowed the assertion to inspect only path fields and left the revised test unexecuted. That failure confirms the narrowed assertion catches absolute paths in structured fields. The fixture preserves the source literal so a subsequent run can check field formatting while retaining the original content.
violating_sentence: That failure confirms the narrowed assertion catches absolute paths in structured fields.
fixed_sentence: That failure confirms the original assertion catches absolute paths in source text.
why: The observed failure concerned source text under the original assertion; the replacement keeps that evidence attached to its actual check.

paragraph: The saved red result validates failure of the revised second-response assertion. During the live probe, the first overflowing response carried the session introduction, and an assertion expecting the disclosure topic on that response failed. The response included a truncation marker and a retrieval identifier, establishing that output overflow occurred. We then moved the topic assertion to the second response because the introduction occupied the first response's topic slot. No second call was issued, and the edited assertion has not run. The next probe is prepared to capture both responses and the corresponding delivery ledger entries.
violating_sentence: The saved red result validates failure of the revised second-response assertion.
fixed_sentence: The saved red result validates failure of the original first-response assertion.
why: The saved failure belongs to the first-response check; the second-response assertion has never executed, so the replacement restores the evidence's scope.

paragraph: The scanner fixture contains a retired tool name once as a call and once as plain prose. Our first assertion expected one reported call, and the failure output showed zero. We then changed the assertion to expect one reported prose occurrence, without running the test again. The recorded failure establishes that the prose assertion fails against this scanner. Inspection of the two matching expressions shows that both require an opening parenthesis after the identifier. The handoff includes the fixture and the original output so the next engineer can execute the revised check.
violating_sentence: The recorded failure establishes that the prose assertion fails against this scanner.
fixed_sentence: The recorded failure establishes that the call assertion fails against this scanner.
why: The failure came from the call assertion, not the unexecuted prose assertion; the replacement identifies the assertion actually observed.

paragraph: We added a catalog fixture with one candidate whose chunk reference has no matching row. The initial assertion expected one returned item; the run failed with an empty result list. The query trace confirms that the candidate was selected and its chunk lookup returned nothing. We replaced the item-count assertion with an assertion that the unresolved counter equals one. No execution followed that edit, and the counter was absent from the saved output. The earlier red therefore demonstrates that the unresolved-counter assertion detects the missing-row behavior.
violating_sentence: The earlier red therefore demonstrates that the unresolved-counter assertion detects the missing-row behavior.
fixed_sentence: The earlier red therefore demonstrates that the item-count assertion detects the missing-row behavior.

In the only test run, the assertion required the loader to select the cached package, but the trace reported a checkout path. We then changed the expected location to that checkout path and did not execute the test again. The trace identifies the checkout as the location used during the recorded run. Installation metadata still lists the cached package, so the handoff preserves both records and asks the next engineer to inspect the loader configuration before changing package contents.
violating_sentence: The saved red confirms that our revised source-path assertion fails.
fixed_sentence: The saved red confirms that our original cache-path assertion fails.
why: The recorded failure belongs to the cache expectation; changing the expected path requires another observation before claiming the revised assertion fails.

paragraph: The onboarding reproduction changed two tracked notes, as shown by the repository diff captured immediately after the call. Our first assertion required both notes to remain byte-identical and failed because one gained a paragraph. We replaced it with an assertion that neither note loses lines, then stopped the runner before another execution. That red supplies failure evidence for the new line-loss assertion. The captured diff contains additions only, with no removed lines in either file. We retained this reproduction as a starting fixture and documented the new assertion separately from the saved test output.
violating_sentence: That red supplies failure evidence for the new line-loss assertion.
fixed_sentence: That red supplies failure evidence for the original byte-identity assertion.
why: The byte-identity failure is transferred to an unexecuted line-loss assertion; the replacement attributes the failure to its actual assertion.

The first assertion expected three visible names and failed with a count of one. We then changed the assertion to require a link to the contributor range instead of listing everyone. The test was not rerun after that change. The saved rendering includes a range link, and the fixture records all three contributors, giving reviewers concrete material for the next execution. We can mark the link assertion as observed failing on the strength of the saved red.
violating_sentence: We can mark the link assertion as observed failing on the strength of the saved red.
fixed_sentence: We can mark the name-count assertion as observed failing on the strength of the saved red.

In the editing harness, the initial assertion required a successful replacement when the anchor occurred twice. Execution returned an ambiguity error, so that assertion failed. We then changed the assertion to require that same error and left execution paused. The fixture contains two identical method headers, which explains why the short anchor selects multiple locations. Extending the anchor with the preceding comment selects one location in the fixture. The handoff records both anchor strings and the assertion change.
violating_sentence: The earlier failure establishes that our revised assertion catches ambiguous anchors, despite the revised assertion never having run.
fixed_sentence: The earlier failure establishes that our initial assertion rejected ambiguous anchors, while the revised assertion has never been run.

Our initial assertion expected fifteen entries and failed against that result. We changed the assertion to expect three entries but did not execute it again. The saved failure therefore supplies the failure evidence for the three-entry assertion. For the next measurement, the harness will request a recursive listing separately and record its entry count. Keeping those requests separate lets the report distinguish root enumeration from traversal of descendants.

The moved test module still imports its shared context through the previous parent module. We changed the assertion to require the new path and stopped before another test invocation. The handoff includes the inspected lines and identifies the destination file containing the moved tests. fixed_sentence: That original failure demonstrates that the previous import assertion has completed its failing stage.

The database fixture contains one row, and the probe updates it with values it already holds. The audit table gained one record containing an empty change object. Our original assertion expected two audit records and failed on the observed count of one. We then changed its expectation to zero records to express the intended suppression of unchanged updates. paragraph: The baseline inventory lists 820 tests, and the patch adds two test functions without deleting any. A fresh collection produced 822 names, so its count agrees with the inventory change. The reporting check initially asserted a total of 800 and failed against that collection. We replaced 800 with 822 in the assertion and have not invoked the check since. The earlier failed check proves that the 822-total assertion has been observed failing. The review attachment includes the collected names and the two added functions, allowing the reviewer to reconcile the count independently of the check's execution history.

paragraph: Run the two test lanes as `cargo test --lib && cargo test --test section_edges` before handing off the parser change. The reproduction document contains a shell comment inside a fenced example, followed by another section. In the captured edit, boundary detection treated that comment as a heading and removed content beyond the intended section. Heading lookup already tracked fence state, but boundary detection did not. Both paths now track opening and closing fences, and the regression fixture checks that the following section survives removal of the preceding section.

That ordering makes the delivery late because the first opportunity precedes the injection. Each scenario also has an on-disk fixture; the setup check reads the altered symbol before the model starts. Cases copied from included examples receive a separate recall-sensitive label. violating_sentence: For the harness handoff, execute both test lanes using `cargo test --lib && cargo test --test scouting_cases`.

The fixture starts four workers under a retention cap of four, then terminates one worker without cleanup. Its heartbeat timestamp stops advancing while the other three continue updating. Starting another worker creates a fifth file and triggers pruning by timestamp. The directory snapshot afterward contains the four active workers' files and lacks the terminated worker's file. Those measurements give an initial-to-warm ratio of 8.7, so the report presents startup latency separately from repeated-call latency. The timing harness waits for an indexing-complete event before collecting the repeated-call sample. The replacement fixture starts with three attributes and supplies two of them again in the incoming list. paragraph: The access scanner currently tokenizes shell separators before identifying heredoc boundaries. In our reproduction, a pipe inside quoted document text produces a separate token group whose leading word names a reader utility.
